1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air in a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein the pump is controlled to reduce parasitic load on an engine while maintaining the established vacuum level.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve that selectively redirects the flow of air to reduce a pressure differential across the pump without allowing the vacuum level to drop below the predetermined value.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device while maintaining a seal in the booster device.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump in a controlled manner to prevent backflow into the booster device.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere through a controlled valve mechanism.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, wherein the filter prevents atmospheric contaminants from entering the pump while the flow is redirected.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to selectively terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value while maintaining the vacuum level, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced and parasitic load on an engine is minimized.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device in a manner that prevents vacuum loss from the booster device.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump with a controlled restriction to prevent backflow.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere through a controlled valve mechanism.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, wherein the filter prevents atmospheric contaminants from entering the pump during redirected flow.

13. (Previously presented) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a braking system with a vacuum servo booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to selectively terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value while maintaining the vacuum level, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device in a manner that prevents vacuum loss from the booster device.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump with a controlled restriction to prevent backflow.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere through a controlled valve mechanism.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, wherein the filter prevents atmospheric contaminants from entering the pump during redirected flow.

19. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Cancelled)
